Title: Fasciculus rerum expetendarum et fugiendarum, prout ab Orthuino Gratio Daventriensi editus
  est, Tomus I (with the appendix of manuscripts first printed here)
Creator: Ortwin Gratius (compiler, 1535); Edward Brown (editor of the 1690 London edition); the
  Brethren of the Unity (the Confession to King Vladislav)
Publisher: Londini: impensis Richardi Chiswell, 1690
Publication Date: 1690
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: Printed at London in 1690 (title page); public domain by the project's date rule
  (published 1930 or earlier). On Internet Archive, the item metadata carries no rights field; that
  tag is supporting evidence only. The scan is a Google Books digitisation hosted on Internet
  Archive; the usage request in its front matter does not claim rights in the public-domain work.
  Checked 2026-09-30.
Language: lat
Source: Internet Archive item bub_gb_Z7e69raCdb8C (archive.org/details/bub_gb_Z7e69raCdb8C),
  full-text OCR file bub_gb_Z7e69raCdb8C_djvu.txt, fetched directly (curl, raw bytes) 2026-09-30 by
  the Library thread; the body below is that file unaltered.
Provenance note: Body unaltered, including its own OCR errors. Header prepended by the Library
  thread. The scan is a Google Books digitisation hosted on Internet Archive; the usage request in
  its front matter does not claim rights in the public-domain work. The 1690 London printing (Brown)
  reprints the 1535 Cologne collection of Ortwin Gratius and adds manuscripts.
Content note: Volume I of Brown's 1690 edition. It prints, under the running head "Ad Vladislaum
  Hung. Reg. missa" (page 163 of the volume), a Latin confession of faith of the Bohemian Brethren
  addressed to King Vladislav, opening "Omnem videlicet fidei veritatem" with a "Professio fidei
  Trinitatis benedictae". The edition's own headings do not settle whether this is the 1504 or the
  1508 text.
